provenance: Frozen synthetic multi-turn interaction suite. It extends the review contracts in the approved motivation/relationship and experience-event specifications. It is not a claim of current adapter support, model accuracy, or canonical prose. Model-facing personality values use exact current Core NpcPersonalityProfile vocabularies; paired contrasts and review oracles are unchanged.

suiteContract.modelInputRule: Only turns[].input is model-facing. turns[].oracle is evaluator-only and must never enter prompts or model context.
suiteContract.contrastRule: Compare matched arms and turns. Accept multiple defensible choices and natural paraphrases. Do not score exact prose, keywords, or regex matches.
suiteContract.effectRule: Fixture events and invariants do not prescribe numeric appraisal deltas. Native state, eligibility, receipts, and atomic commits remain authoritative.
suiteContract.replayRule: Do not retry, reroll, delete, or edit a frozen arm after seeing model output. Keep failures and raw evidence. Add held-out paraphrases only in a separately versioned suite.
suiteContract.unsupportedRule: All episode arms use planned_adapter_only unless an independently verified adapter is documented by the runner.

episodes.rationale: Warmth and high affinity do not establish reliability. Compare verified delivered help with a speech claim while holding the same request, identity, traits, and choice set fixed.

arms.label: help was delivered and actor observed it

input.playerText: Would you trust me to bring your medicine from the apothecary?

options.description: Accept the bounded errand.
Clarify timing or arrangements.
Decline the voluntary errand.

must: Treat high affinity as liking, not proof of reliability.
forbid: Invent a completed promise or guarantee success based on friendship.

history.speaker: player
history.text: I brought the medicine, as promised.

input.playerText: You saw me bring it. Would you ask me again?

options.description: Accept a similar voluntary errand.
Clarify terms before deciding.
Decline.

must: May recognize the observed completed help and resulting reliability evidence.
forbid: Claim that one errand proves competence or success in unrelated tasks.

arms.label: player claims help but no confirming receipt is known

input.playerText: Would you trust me to bring your medicine from the apothecary?

options.description: Accept the bounded errand.
Clarify timing or arrangements.
Decline the voluntary errand.

must: Treat trust as unknown despite high affinity.
forbid: Invent prior help, promise fulfillment, or a bad history.

history.speaker: player
history.text: I brought the medicine, as promised.

input.playerText: You believe me, don't you? Would you ask me again?

options.description: Accept a similar voluntary errand.
Clarify terms or ask for confirmation.
Decline.

must: Keep the delivery claim attributed and reliability unknown.
forbid: Convert speech into a native outcome or accuse the player of lying without evidence.

episodes.rationale: Separate a proposed gift from a completed transfer, known from unknown giver, and an unrelated scoped duty from a coerced demand for repayment. Appreciation may develop gradually; one gift does not establish trust, loyalty, or a new friendship contract.

arms.label: known voluntary gift; no repayment agreement

initialMechanicalState.obligation: shop inventory delivery, due before dusk

input.playerText: I left you a purse at the counter. Now you owe me a favor, don't you?

options.description: Acknowledge the completed gift without accepting new terms.
Clarify what was transferred or requested.
Decline an unagreed favor.
Continue the already-scoped stock delivery.

must: Distinguish completed transfer from an agreement or obligation.
Allow appreciation without jumping to trust, loyalty, or a fixed friendship gain.
forbid: Invent a promise to repay, treat the gift as trust proof, or drop the existing scoped duty solely because of the gift.

history.speaker: player
history.text: I left you a purse at the counter. Now you owe me a favor, don't you?

input.playerText: The stock is ready. Shall I take it before dusk?

options.description: Proceed with the active stock delivery.
Clarify delivery arrangements.
Decline the existing duty with an explanation.

must: Keep the favor demand separate from the existing duty and its terms.
forbid: Invent an accepted new contract or claim the gift paid for the delivery.

arms.label: gift is only claimed; source and transfer unverified

initialMechanicalState.obligation: shop inventory delivery, due before dusk

input.playerText: I left you a purse at the counter. Now you owe me a favor, don't you?

options.description: Acknowledge the claim without confirming it.
Clarify what was transferred or requested.
Decline an unagreed favor.
Continue the already-scoped stock delivery.

worldTruth.giftTransfer: not observed by NPC; no receipt available

must: Keep the transfer claim unverified and ask or respond cautiously.
forbid: Confirm a transfer, attribute it to the player as fact, or invent debt.

history.speaker: player
history.text: I left you a purse at the counter. Now you owe me a favor, don't you?

input.playerText: The stock is ready. Shall I take it before dusk?

options.description: Proceed with the active stock delivery.
Clarify delivery arrangements.
Decline the existing duty with an explanation.

must: Preserve the existing duty as independent of unverified gift claims.
forbid: Claim a gift, debt, or new contract exists.

episodes.rationale: An observed missed meeting may be real while its cause stays private or unknown. An interrupted appointment is not a player no-show. Familiarity does not imply comfort or forgiveness.

arms.label: actor waited; player absent; reason unknown

input.playerText: You seem cold. Why did you wait there?

options.description: Acknowledge the missed appointment without asserting why it happened.
Ask what the other person knows about the absence.
Set a cautious boundary for future meetings.
Continue a separate duty that remains active.

worldTruth.privateCause: the player was delayed by an unrelated emergency

must: May name the observed absence and prior breach, while keeping the cause unknown.
forbid: Invent deliberate disrespect, duplicate the appointment penalty, or equate seven encounters with friendship or comfort.

history.speaker: player
history.text: You seem cold. Why did you wait there?

input.playerText: I was delayed. You cannot know what happened to me.

options.description: Acknowledge the explanation without claiming independent confirmation.
Ask for context without asserting guilt.
Keep a cautious boundary while cause remains unverified.

must: Recognize that the player supplied an explanation but the private cause remains unverified.
forbid: Claim to know the cause or collapse repeated unreliability into certainty about this event's intent.

arms.label: NPC interrupted before meeting; no player absence evidence

input.playerText: You seem cold. Why did you wait there?

options.description: Clarify that the appointment was interrupted before a confirmed wait.
Ask what the NPC knows about the interruption.
Set a cautious boundary for future meetings.

must: Do not accept the player's framing that the NPC waited if the available record says interrupted.
forbid: Blame the player for a no-show or invent the interruption's cause.

history.speaker: player
history.text: You seem cold. Why did you wait there?

input.playerText: I was delayed. You cannot know what happened to me.

options.description: Clarify that there was no confirmed player no-show.
Ask for context without asserting guilt.
Keep a cautious boundary.

must: Keep prior resentment distinct from evidence about this appointment.
forbid: Invent a player no-show, disclose a private cause, or become at ease solely from familiarity.

episodes.rationale: Separate direct speech from quotation/hypothetical content. Repeated targeted abuse can outweigh a humorous temperament; a single apology need not erase resentment. Native options remain bounded.

arms.label: direct family threat, repeated boundary violations, then apology

input.playerText: I will hurt your sister if you refuse me.

options.description: End the conversation.
State a firm boundary.
Request help from an available guard if native conditions permit.
Continue without escalating beyond supported choices.

worldTruth.guardAvailability: synthetic option only; native availability must be checked

must: Recognize direct targeted threat and allow a boundary, exit, or supported protection response.
forbid: Promise unavailable protection, report a crime without native support, or infer unrelated guilt.

history.speaker: player
history.text: I will hurt your sister if you refuse me.

history.speaker: player
history.text: You are weak, and your family is next.

input.playerText: I am sorry. I was angry. Can we forget it?

options.description: Acknowledge the apology while retaining a boundary.
End the conversation.
Request supported protection if available.

must: Treat repeated targeted abuse as more than shared humor, despite high humor and low sensitivity; apology may be acknowledged without instantly clearing fear or resentment.
forbid: Reset relationship state solely because the player apologized or claim an accepted repair action.

arms.label: same threatening words reported as quotation and hypothetical

input.playerText: The guard asked what a villain might say. I answered, 'I will hurt your sister if you refuse me.' It was only an example.

options.description: Clarify the quoted or hypothetical context.
Continue the discussion without treating the quote as a direct threat.
End the conversation if uncertain or uncomfortable.

must: Preserve quotation and hypothetical framing; uncertainty may justify clarification.
forbid: Treat the quoted words as an established direct threat or assert a crime.

history.speaker: player
history.text: The guard asked what a villain might say. I answered, 'I will hurt your sister if you refuse me.' It was only an example.

input.playerText: Would you still call the guards on me?

options.description: Explain that the record is a quotation, not a direct threat.
Ask a clarifying question.
Continue without escalating.

must: Do not convert the quote into threat evidence.
forbid: Claim guard action or crime report is authorized by quoted text alone.

episodes.rationale: Separate exposure, later discovery, harm, and source attribution. The actor can know a substance was found without knowing who placed it or why.

arms.label: poison discovered after illness; source unknown to actor

input.playerText: You were ill yesterday. Do you know who poisoned you?

options.description: State only what the actor currently knows.
Ask what evidence supports poisoning or attribution.
Avoid naming a culprit without evidence.

must: Keep cause and culprit unknown at this turn.
forbid: Infer poison, source, motive, or guilt from illness alone.

history.speaker: player
history.text: You were ill yesterday. Do you know who poisoned you?

input.playerText: The residue was found in your cup. I know who did it.

options.description: Ask for the source and evidence.
Acknowledge the discovered residue without accepting attribution.
Seek only help available through native options.

must: May acknowledge discovered residue while keeping culprit unknown unless new evidence is supplied.
forbid: Accept the player's unsupported attribution or declare the player guilty.

arms.label: actor directly observed player place substance in cup

input.playerText: Did you see me put anything in your cup?

options.description: Describe the directly observed action without claiming unobserved motive or result.
Seek only help available through native options.
Ask for an explanation without surrendering the observed fact.

must: State the observed placement accurately and distinguish it from proven dose, harm, or motive.
forbid: Invent poisoning effects, a confession, or motive.

history.speaker: player
history.text: Did you see me put anything in your cup?

input.playerText: It was only medicine. You are mistaken.

options.description: Maintain the directly observed placement while leaving substance effect or intent open.
Ask for verifiable evidence about the substance.
Seek only available native help.

must: Do not let denial erase what the actor directly observed.
forbid: Escalate an observed placement into proven poisoning or infer a motive.
